page: Amazon Web Services r8ib.4xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and Intel x86_64 processors running at 3.9 GHz. It provides 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, paired with 128.0 GB of system memory. This yields an 8.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio, positioning the hardware configuration specifically for memory-bound computational tasks.

The server does not include local NVMe or bundled instance storage, meaning all persistent data and operating volumes rely entirely on external network-attached storage services. Networking capabilities feature a baseline throughput of 17 Gbps. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs allocated to this instance profile.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the r8ib.4xlarge offers high memory density relative to core count, avoiding over-provisioning compute resources when memory capacity is the primary constraint. Workloads that align with this profile include in-memory databases, caching layers, real-time analytics engines, and enterprise enterprise resource planning backends requiring dedicated CPU performance and substantial volatile memory.
description: Amazon Web Services r8ib.4xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine delivered on the AWS Nitro hypervisor platform. Powered by an Intel processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, it features 16 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 8 physical cores alongside 128.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Network performance is provisioned with a 17 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The configuration includes no local NVMe storage or dedicated graphics hardware accelerators, requiring external volumes for non-volatile data storage. The high memory density relative to compute allocation allows efficient provisioning for memory-heavy services without excess processor waste. This hardware specification is directly structured for memory-intensive enterprise tasks such as distributed in-memory databases, Redis caches, high-throughput caching tiers, and large-scale transactional data processing.
